name: Creator Assistant Links
author: Alessandro Lioce

sections.description:
An article you write today should link to the one you write tomorrow. Creator Assistant Links finds, for every article, the other articles of your site that go deeper into what it discusses, and links them from the right words of the text.

  • Works on every article, also the ones you wrote before installing it.
  • Links are recomputed when an article is published or changed, and only for the articles it concerns.
  • Links are added when the content is shown: on the site, in feeds and in the REST API. They are never saved into your content, so they can change at any time, and deactivating the plugin removes them all.
  • An article that is unpublished stops receiving links at once; published again, its links come back.
  • In the block editor, the automatic links are highlighted and listed in the “Automatic links” panel, where you can exclude any of them for good.

Requirements

  • Creator Assistant Hub 1.2.0 or higher, with OpenAI and Qdrant configured. This plugin uses the content injection API the Hub publishes since 1.2.0: update the Hub first, because WordPress cannot express a minimum version in Requires Plugins. With an older Hub the plugin stays idle and shows a notice. With Hub 1.4.0 or higher the links are chosen with the Hub’s “reasoning” model profile; an older Hub keeps gpt-5.4-mini.
  • WordPress 6.8 or higher.
  • PHP 7.4 or higher.

After a group of articles is published, the plugin waits two hours without new articles before computing the links, so articles written together are linked once. To skip the wait, use “Process the queue now” in Creator Assistant → Links.

Part of the Creator Assistant family

  • Creator Assistant Hub connects your site to OpenAI and Qdrant (required).
  • Creator Assistant Search adds AI search to your site.
  • Creator Assistant Knowledge answers questions from private knowledge.

External services

This plugin uses the services configured in Creator Assistant Hub, and only after you accepted its terms there.

  • OpenAI: turning this plugin on also turns on two Hub features, which are off by default. Hub’s content vectorization sends the text of your articles to OpenAI to create embeddings, and Hub’s article summaries are generated with OpenAI. To choose the links, the plugin also sends OpenAI the title, the language and the paragraphs of the article being linked, and the titles, summaries and passages of the candidate articles. Terms, privacy policy.
  • Qdrant: the vectors of the text of your articles, created by Hub’s vectorization, are stored in Qdrant, and the plugin searches them to find the candidate articles. Terms, privacy policy.

Development

The source files for all compiled assets are included in the plugin: the block-editor panel is under src/ and is compiled to build/.

Build tools required: Node.js (includes npm).

  1. Install dependencies: npm install
  2. Build the block-editor panel: npm run build (uses @wordpress/scripts)

Source files are in src/ and compiled to build/.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Creator Assistant Hub 1.2.0 or higher, then accept its terms and enter your OpenAI and Qdrant details in Creator Assistant → Hub.
  2. Upload the creator-assistant-links folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the plugin directly from the WordPress plugin screen.
  3. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  4. The published articles are queued automatically. The links are computed after the quiet period (two hours by default); to skip the wait, open Creator Assistant → Links and press “Process the queue now”.
  5. Open an article in the block editor and use the “Automatic links” panel to see its links or exclude one.
sections.faq:
How much does it cost?

One OpenAI request per article the first time the plugin is activated. When you deactivate and activate it again, only the articles published or edited in the meantime are processed again. After that, one per article each time links need to change. An article whose paragraphs and candidates did not change is not sent again, except when you recalculate by hand (the editor’s button or “Recalculate every article” in the settings): a manual recalculation always sends the request. The vectorization of Hub (embeddings and article summaries) has a cost of its own, which is not included here.

My page cache shows old links

The plugin clears WordPress’s post cache when links change. A page cache plugin may keep the old page until it expires.

Can I change the waits and limits?

Yes, with filters: creator_assistant_links_post_types, creator_assistant_links_similarity_threshold, creator_assistant_links_targets_per_chunk, creator_assistant_links_max_candidates, creator_assistant_links_max_links, creator_assistant_links_anchor_word_limits, creator_assistant_links_quiet_period, creator_assistant_links_max_wait, creator_assistant_links_vectorization_wait_cap, creator_assistant_links_batch_size, creator_assistant_links_lock_timeout, creator_assistant_links_candidate_filter, creator_assistant_links_llm_options (model, reasoning effort, timeout and output budget; default the Hub’s “reasoning” profile, gpt-6-luna with medium effort), creator_assistant_links_article_language( $locale, $post ) (the language of an article, which decides the language of the link texts; defaults to the site locale).
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: with Creator Assistant Hub 1.4.0 or higher, the link plan is an OpenAI feature of the Hub (“Internal link plan”), so Creator Assistant Hub Pro can choose its model; the creator_assistant_links_llm_options filter receives that choice as the default and still has the last word.
  • Changed: the links are chosen with the “reasoning” model profile of Creator Assistant Hub 1.4.0 or higher (gpt-6-luna with medium effort) instead of gpt-5.4-mini, so a model update only needs a Hub update. With an older Hub the plugin keeps gpt-5.4-mini. The creator_assistant_links_llm_options filter receives the profile, with its output budget, as the default.

1.0.0

  • First version.

upgrade_notice.1.1.0: Update Creator Assistant Hub to 1.4.0 first: with it the links are chosen with the model of the Hub's reasoning profile, kept current by Hub updates. With an older Hub the plugin keeps using gpt-5.4-mini.

screenshots.caption: The Creator Assistant → Links screen: the articles waiting for their links, the active and excluded links, and the buttons to process the queue or recalculate every article.

The block editor with the "Automatic links" panel open: the words that will be linked are highlighted in the text, and the panel lists each link with its target article, its text and its state, so you can exclude any of them.
The result on the site: an article with the links inside its text, as a visitor sees them.
